title: Technical English — Course 3, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 11

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the revision-symbol lesson take place?
tasks.audioText: The drawing office will review revision symbols on Thursday at ten fifteen. Students should meet in the design classroom and bring the assembly drawing from the course folder. The tutor will explain how revision letters, change notes and issue dates help readers identify the current drawing. Students will compare two printed versions and list the visible changes.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which drawing should students bring?
tasks.audioText: The drawing office will review revision symbols on Thursday at ten fifteen. Students should meet in the design classroom and bring the assembly drawing from the course folder. The tutor will explain how revision letters, change notes and issue dates help readers identify the current drawing. Students will compare two printed versions and list the visible changes.
options: The assembly drawing from the course folder

tasks.prompt: A revised engineering drawing may include a new revision identifier, an updated issue date and a description of the changes. A reader should check these details before using dimensions or component references. If two copies appear different, the document register can help establish which version is current and approved. Old copies should be clearly identified to prevent accidental use. Reading 1. Which details may identify a revised drawing?
options: Revision identifier, issue date and description of changes

tasks.prompt: Where can a reader check which version is current?
The latest drawing revision ___ in the document register.
Choose TWO details that help identify a controlled drawing revision.
options: The colour of the drawing folder
The name of an unrelated website

tasks.prompt: A short description of changes made to a drawing is a revision ___.
Two drawing copies show different revision letters. What should you ask?
options: I will use the one with more dimensions.
Could we check the document register to confirm the current approved revision?
The revision letter does not matter.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of technical drawing revisions in a logical order.
options: Confirm the current approved copy in the register
Check the revision identifier and issue date
correctOrder: Check the revision identifier and issue date
Confirm the current approved copy in the register

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words explaining how revision identifiers, issue dates and change notes help control technical drawings.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: task completion and relevant content (0–2); clear organisation and logical linking (0–2); grammar and sentence structure (0–2); accurate technical vocabulary, spelling and punctuation (0–2). Minor errors are acceptable if meaning remains clear.
